text: FSB Arrests Moldovan Suspected of Shooting Air Force General Sep. 8, 2026 The Russian Investigative Committee Russia’s FSB security service said Tuesday that it arrested a Moldovan man who is suspected of shooting a Russian Aerospace Forces general on behalf of Ukraine last week. The FSB said its agents in the southern Astrakhan region arrested the man, identified as 21-year-old Nicolae Cociu. Investigators claim that Cociu shot a Russian serviceman near the Saratov region city of Engels last Thursday. While authorities did not identify the Russian serviceman by name, pro-Kremlin media reported last week that Major General Nikolai Varpakhovich, who heads a strategic bomber division at Engels-2 airbase, was shot and wounded in the Saratov region. In an official statement, the Investigative Committee, Russia’s top investigative body, confirmed the armed attack against the officer, who was hospitalized after receiving six gunshot wounds. title: Australian politics live: Albanese makes ‘no apology’ for $6m golf club grant in own electorate; Victorian bills may rise by $100 under Coalition
text: 18.16 EDT Albanese makes ‘no apology’ for $6m grant to Marrickville golf club Anthony Albanese has defended a grant handed to a golf club in his electorate, and said he makes “no apology” for it. The grant was part of an infrastructure program that disbursed most of its money to safe, marginal or target Labor seats. Over on ABC News Breakfast, Albanese says there were three grants in that program handed to his seat, and the funding for the golf club was to stop sewage from the course going into the local river during rain events. He then attacks the ABC. The ABC were told information they chose not to publish appropriately … because it is on a flood area by the Cooks River, when it rains and there’s flooding, raw sewerage goes into the Cooks River. That’s what it’s for – for fixing that. I make no apologies for my electorate being serviced by me as a good local member , these three grants, they’re all appropriate. Albanese also confirms he was made an honorary member of the club some 15 years ago, but doesn’t say whether he should have declared it. I don’t have a card. I don’t go in there. I haven’t been in there for years. I used to walk my dog along the path.
author: Krishani Dhanji

title: US supreme court rejects Missouri Republicans’ appeal to use Trump-backed congressional map in midterms – live
text: 17.41 EDT Supreme court rebuffs Missouri's push to use redrawn congressional map in November The US supreme court will not suspend a ruling from Missouri’s highest state court that prevented the use of a Donald Trump-backed US House map in an upcoming election. Last week the state’s supreme court ruled that the map must go before voters to approve or reject the new districts, meaning it cannot be used in the November election. Trump and Republicans fumed over the decision, with the president calling it “horrible, ridiculous, and unConstitutional”. Catherine Hanaway, the state’s Republican attorney general, immediately pledged to appeal to the supreme court. The conservative Justice Brett Kavanaugh denied the emergency request.

title: North Korea and Russia open first road bridge linking both countries
text: North Korea and Russia open first road bridge linking both countries Image source, Reuters Image caption, The road spans the Tumen river connecting the border cities of Rason and Khasan. By Jake Kwon Seoul Correspondent Published 8 September 2026 The first road bridge linking Russia and North Korea has opened, allowing the two countries to more easily move cargo and passengers between their border across the Tumen river. Pyongyang state media said the bridge will be used for "personnel exchanges, tourism and trade". But Ukrainian investigative organisation Truth Hounds said the bridge is intended "primarily to establish a covert military logistics corridor" to support Russia in the Ukraine war. It comes amid stronger ties between the countries since the start of the Ukraine war, with Russia's Putin and North Korea's Kim Jong Un previously pledging that they would help each other in the event of "aggression" against either country. Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin described the bridge as a "new symbol of friendship", while North Korea's Prime Minister Pak Thae Song said it was a "historical event". title: Ukraine's chief prosecutor resigns over call centre corruption scandal
text: Ukraine's chief prosecutor resigns over call centre corruption scandal Image source, Reuters By Tabby Wilson Published 8 September 2026 Ukraine's chief prosecutor Ruslan Kravchenko has resigned over corruption allegations related to illegal call centres in the country. It follows a search of his offices over the weekend by Ukrainian anti-corruption investigators, who said they had identified a money-laundering scheme led by an official in Kravchenko's office. In his resignation letter, Kravchenko said he did not want his position to be used as a "tool for political confrontation", and referenced an earlier post in which he rejected the claims as "unsubstantiated". Corruption scandals have plagued Kyiv throughout the war against Russia, with accusations levelled at several members of President Volodymyr Zelensky's inner circle. According to Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau (Nabu) and Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (Sap), the network in Kravchenko's office received money to protect call centres that carried out phone scams and "laundered millions in assets". Russia’s Central Bank announced Tuesday that Matyukhin passed away on Saturday, one day ahead of his 92nd birthday. The regulator praised Matyukhin as an “active and responsible leader” who was appointed to lead the State Bank of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic “during a critical turning point” in 1990. “He oversaw the formation of the Bank of Russia under new conditions, leading it until 1992,” the Central Bank said in a statement. opinion How Russia’s Obsession With Economic Stability Made It Weaker Read more Matyukhin played a key role in the development of modern Russia’s financial sector during severe currency shortages and soaring inflation. Russian business media described one of his main achievements as the establishment of Russia’s two-tiered banking system, with separated central monetary authority from commercial banking operations. title: Hungary Expels 10 Russian Diplomats for ‘Unacceptable Activities’
text: Hungary Expels 10 Russian Diplomats for ‘Unacceptable Activities’ By AFP and Reuters Sep. 8, 2026 The Russian Embassy in Budapest. Aled Betts (CC BY 2.0) Hungary expelled 10 Russia n diplomats on Tuesday, saying they had acted in ways incompatible with their diplomatic status. Those kicked out "were engaged in activities in Hungary that are unacceptable for diplomats under the Vienna Convention," Hungarian Foreign Minister Anita Orban said in an emailed statement on Tuesday. Hungary has "called on the individuals in question to leave" the country, Orban said. She added that the action "does not imply breaking off diplomatic relations with Russia." "Hungary intends to continue the necessary dialogue, based on mutual respect and adherence to the rules," Orban said, without giving details of what the mission staffers had allegedly done. Russia 's Foreign Ministry said it would retaliate for the expulsion of its diplomats. "The response to the Russophobic lobby in Budapest will be harsh and painful," Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova told the state-run news agency TASS. title: Finland Completes Construction of Russian Border Fence
text: Finland Completes Construction of Russian Border Fence Sep. 8, 2026 The new border fence between Finland and Russia. raja.fi Finland has completed construction on a 200-kilometer (124-mile) fence along its eastern border with Russia, three years after the project began, the Finnish public broadcaster Yle reported Monday. Finnish Interior Minister Mari Rantanen presented the completed fence near a shuttered border crossing, saying the barrier addresses heightened security risks following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and could be extended further. “What we particularly need is EU funding for eastern member states so that projects like this can be financed,” Rantanen said. The new fence cost 356 million euros ($413 million), with an estimated 2-3 million euros for annual maintenance, according to Finnish border authorities. news Tension and Unease for Russians in Finland Amid Border Shutdown Read more The barbed wire fence spans Finland’s southeastern border with Russia and parts of its eastern flank. title: FSB Arrests Moldovan Suspected of Shooting Air Force General
text: FSB Arrests Moldovan Suspected of Shooting Air Force General Sep. 8, 2026 The Russian Investigative Committee Russia’s FSB security service said Tuesday that it arrested a Moldovan man who is suspected of shooting a Russian Aerospace Forces general on behalf of Ukraine last week. The FSB said its agents in the southern Astrakhan region arrested the man, identified as 21-year-old Nicolae Cociu. Investigators claim that Cociu shot a Russian serviceman near the Saratov region city of Engels last Thursday. While authorities did not identify the Russian serviceman by name, pro-Kremlin media reported last week that Major General Nikolai Varpakhovich, who heads a strategic bomber division at Engels-2 airbase, was shot and wounded in the Saratov region. In an official statement, the Investigative Committee, Russia’s top investigative body, confirmed the armed attack against the officer, who was hospitalized after receiving six gunshot wounds. A 39-year-old man was killed in an attack on a gas station in the Bryansk region town of Starodub, 35 kilometers (21 miles) north of the Ukrainian border, acting Governor Yegor Kovalchuk said . Three others were wounded, he added. In the nearby Belgorod region, acting Governor Alexander Shuvayev said one person was killed in a border district as a result of a “targeted” hit. Four others were injured across the region, where Shuvayev said Ukraine carried out 112 attacks in the past 24 hours. Unverified reports said that Ukrainian drones targeted a Rosneft-operated oil refinery in the southern Saratov region. title: Germany Says It Is Closing a Russian Cultural Center. That Might Not Be So Simple.
text: Germany Says It Is Closing a Russian Cultural Center. That Might Not Be So Simple. By Ned Garvey Sep. 8, 2026 Supporters of Germany's Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) party demonstrate in support of the Russian House in Berlin. REUTERS / Liesa Johannssen BERLIN — On a rainy Friday evening in Germany’s capital, hundreds of people gathered to protest the government’s announcement that it was terminating the lease of the Russian House, a Russian cultural center owned and operated by Moscow. Demonstrators called on the government to reverse its decision, end its “russophobia” and stop what they called its constant “aggression” toward Russia. “It’s the only place left for cultural exchange,” a protester told The Moscow Times, declining to give their name. Down the street, a dozen or so supporters of Russia’s liberal opposition chanted slogans like “Russia without Putin” and held signs up with phrases like “The Kremlin shouldn’t have an address in Berlin.” A bit further away, roughly 100 pro-Ukraine activists held up boxes that symbolized suitcases and bore slogans like “Suitcase, train station, Moscow,” and spoke about their efforts to close the Russian House dating back to 2022. title: Russian Postal Workers to Arm Themselves With Anti-Drone Weapons
text: Russian Postal Workers to Arm Themselves With Anti-Drone Weapons Sep. 8, 2026 An anti‑drone gun. Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency The Russian government has authorized federal postal service employees to carry anti-drone weapons as Ukraine ramps up its attacks across the country. “Special technical means of countering unmanned aerial, underwater and surface vessels and vehicles, autonomous land vehicles and other automated unmanned systems” have been added to an official list of weapons, ammunition and special gear. A 2005 government decree already allows postal employees to carry 9mm pistols, as well as stun guns and body armor. These weapons are typically given to security staff transporting cash. The expanded decree signed by Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin last Thursday does not specify which Russian Post workers will receive the anti-drone weapons. news Can ‘Russia’s Amazon’ Survive Ukraine’s Drone Campaign? By Ned Garvey Sep. 8, 2026 Supporters of Germany's Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) party demonstrate in support of the Russian House in Berlin. REUTERS / Liesa Johannssen BERLIN — On a rainy Friday evening in Germany’s capital, hundreds of people gathered to protest the government’s announcement that it was terminating the lease of the Russian House, a Russian cultural center owned and operated by Moscow. Demonstrators called on the government to reverse its decision, end its “russophobia” and stop what they called its constant “aggression” toward Russia. “It’s the only place left for cultural exchange,” a protester told The Moscow Times, declining to give their name. Down the street, a dozen or so supporters of Russia’s liberal opposition chanted slogans like “Russia without Putin” and held signs up with phrases like “The Kremlin shouldn’t have an address in Berlin.” A bit further away, roughly 100 pro-Ukraine activists held up boxes that symbolized suitcases and bore slogans like “Suitcase, train station, Moscow,” and spoke about their efforts to close the Russian House dating back to 2022. title: Russian Postal Workers to Arm Themselves With Anti-Drone Weapons
text: Russian Postal Workers to Arm Themselves With Anti-Drone Weapons Sep. 8, 2026 An anti‑drone gun. Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency The Russian government has authorized federal postal service employees to carry anti-drone weapons as Ukraine ramps up its attacks across the country. “Special technical means of countering unmanned aerial, underwater and surface vessels and vehicles, autonomous land vehicles and other automated unmanned systems” have been added to an official list of weapons, ammunition and special gear. A 2005 government decree already allows postal employees to carry 9mm pistols, as well as stun guns and body armor. These weapons are typically given to security staff transporting cash. text: Georgy Matyukhin, Russia’s First Central Bank Chief, Dies at 91 Sep. 8, 2026 Georgy Matyukhin. wikimedia.org The first governor of Russia’s Central Bank after the fall of the Soviet Union, Georgy Matyukhin, has died at the age of 91. title: Hungary Expels 10 Russian Diplomats for ‘Unacceptable Activities’
text: Hungary Expels 10 Russian Diplomats for ‘Unacceptable Activities’ By AFP and Reuters Sep. 8, 2026 The Russian Embassy in Budapest. Aled Betts (CC BY 2.0) Hungary expelled 10 Russia n diplomats on Tuesday, saying they had acted in ways incompatible with their diplomatic status. Those kicked out "were engaged in activities in Hungary that are unacceptable for diplomats under the Vienna Convention," Hungarian Foreign Minister Anita Orban said in an emailed statement on Tuesday. Hungary has "called on the individuals in question to leave" the country, Orban said. She added that the action "does not imply breaking off diplomatic relations with Russia." "Hungary intends to continue the necessary dialogue, based on mutual respect and adherence to the rules," Orban said, without giving details of what the mission staffers had allegedly done. Russia 's Foreign Ministry said it would retaliate for the expulsion of its diplomats. "The response to the Russophobic lobby in Budapest will be harsh and painful," Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova told the state-run news agency TASS. title: Finland Completes Construction of Russian Border Fence
text: Finland Completes Construction of Russian Border Fence Sep. 8, 2026 The new border fence between Finland and Russia. raja.fi Finland has completed construction on a 200-kilometer (124-mile) fence along its eastern border with Russia, three years after the project began, the Finnish public broadcaster Yle reported Monday. Finnish Interior Minister Mari Rantanen presented the completed fence near a shuttered border crossing, saying the barrier addresses heightened security risks following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and could be extended further. “What we particularly need is EU funding for eastern member states so that projects like this can be financed,” Rantanen said. The new fence cost 356 million euros ($413 million), with an estimated 2-3 million euros for annual maintenance, according to Finnish border authorities. news Tension and Unease for Russians in Finland Amid Border Shutdown Read more The barbed wire fence spans Finland’s southeastern border with Russia and parts of its eastern flank. title: FSB Arrests Moldovan Suspected of Shooting Air Force General
text: FSB Arrests Moldovan Suspected of Shooting Air Force General Sep. 8, 2026 The Russian Investigative Committee Russia’s FSB security service said Tuesday that it arrested a Moldovan man who is suspected of shooting a Russian Aerospace Forces general on behalf of Ukraine last week. The FSB said its agents in the southern Astrakhan region arrested the man, identified as 21-year-old Nicolae Cociu. Investigators claim that Cociu shot a Russian serviceman near the Saratov region city of Engels last Thursday. While authorities did not identify the Russian serviceman by name, pro-Kremlin media reported last week that Major General Nikolai Varpakhovich, who heads a strategic bomber division at Engels-2 airbase, was shot and wounded in the Saratov region. In an official statement, the Investigative Committee, Russia’s top investigative body, confirmed the armed attack against the officer, who was hospitalized after receiving six gunshot wounds. title: US bans Canadian dairy, alcohol and motorcycles as trade war escalates
text: The US and Canada have long sparred over trade, particularly Canada’s protected dairy market and its subsidies for producers of softwood lumber. Сергій «Борцуха» на цьому фото - боєць групи снайперів «Тенгрі» ГУР МО у перші дні великого вторгнення з гранатометом та трьома пострілами до РПГ-7 їде по мосту в Ірпінь, щоб зупинити на велосипеді російські бронетанкові колони у десятки кілометрів довжиною, які рвались на Гостомель, Ірпінь та Бучу. Хаос, паніка, страх, кинуті машини, біженці тікають, але знайшлись ті, хто попри все пішли назустріч смертельній загрозі. Велосипеди та гранатомети проти танків, авіації, балістичних ракет - так це було, і воля, характер, масовий героїзм кращих людей, який рвались у бій, змінили хід битви та хід світової історії на користь України. Фото зробив воін-доброволець групи «Тенгрі» Володимир Миронюк WM Blood , позивний Джон. «Тенгрі» - найрезультативніший та найвідоміший в діючий армії снайпер, зібрав кращих бійців, які мали великий досвід війни на Донбасі, і повів їх у бій за Київ. title: Romania detains a Russian man accused of scouting military bases used by NATO allies and critical infrastructure for an alleged sabotage plot
text: Romanian authorities have detained a 40-year-old Russian citizen suspected of plotting an act of sabotage in the country, according to Romanian news outlet Digi24 . The Romanian Intelligence Service said the man had been under surveillance since February 2026. As part of the alleged sabotage plot, he followed instructions from an intermediary and photographed Romanian military equipment, military bases used by NATO allies, communications hubs, and critical infrastructure sites. He also filmed Ukrainian Antonov cargo aircraft while they were in Romania. The intelligence service said the suspect’s methods resembled those used elsewhere in Europe by sabotage networks coordinated by Russian entities. The intelligence service said it thwarted the plot in cooperation with other agencies, including intelligence services in partner countries. Authorities have not named the detainee. Newsweek Romania identified him as Ivan Kutsenko. Agentstvo, which reviewed leaked records, said Kutsenko is from Novosibirsk. title: Russian political prisoner Alexey Gorinov says he may have been poisoned as Moscow City Court rejects his lawyer’s bid to reopen his case
text: Former Moscow municipal deputy Alexey Gorinov said at a Moscow City Court hearing that he may have been poisoned, according to the Telegram news channel SotaVision . He took part in the hearing by video link from a penal colony in Altai Krai. The court considered an appeal against prosecutors’ refusal to reopen the criminal case against Gorinov and ultimately upheld that refusal. The political prisoner told the court that prison officials were not registering his requests for medical care. He asked the court to help him obtain treatment, but the court refused. Gorinov was among the first Russians convicted under the law criminalizing “false information” about the military. In 2022, he was sentenced to seven years in a penal colony after proposing a moment of silence at a municipal council meeting “for the victims of the ongoing military aggression in Ukraine.” He later received an additional prison term in a separate “justifying terrorism” case based on conversations with fellow inmates. title: 69 Russians return home as ‘Professor Molchanov’ remains impounded in Norway over a claim by Ukraine’s Naftogaz
text: Sixty-nine Russian citizens who were aboard the Professor Molchanov , which was impounded in Norway several days ago, have returned home, the governor of Svalbard said. The Russians had originally been scheduled to return home aboard the impounded vessel. Instead, the governor “assisted” with their return ahead of schedule “after good cooperation” with the Russian consul general in Barentsburg and representatives of the Arktikugol trust. Alexey Chekunkov, Russia’s minister for the development of the Far East and Arctic, said Russia “will continue working to secure the release of the Professor Molchanov , which was illegally detained by Norwegian authorities.” A court ordered the Professor Molchanov impounded on September 2 after granting a claim filed by Ukraine’s Naftogaz. According to the governor of Svalbard’s website, the seizure was part of Naftogaz’s effort to recover funds expropriated by Russia in 2014. At the time, the governor said the vessel would remain moored in Barentsburg until further notice and that the authorities, together with the Arktikugol trust, would take care of the crew and passengers aboard. She frames the war in the Persian Gulf as a mutually damaging stalemate in which neither Washington nor Tehran has found a politically sustainable exit: "There are no winners in this war". Her central argument is that the conflict has created a problem of face-saving as much as military strategy. The US faces rising economic and electoral costs, while Iran confronts shortages, inflation, domestic dissent and intensified repression. Neither side, in her assessment, can plausibly claim success. Ushakov added that Trump emphasized the “enormous benefits” of developing U.S.-Russian trade and economic ties. “Donald Trump is interested in achieving a breakthrough during his presidency,” he said. text: Russian Postal Workers to Arm Themselves With Anti-Drone Weapons Sep. 8, 2026 An anti‑drone gun. Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency The Russian government has authorized federal postal service employees to carry anti-drone weapons as Ukraine ramps up its attacks across the country. “Special technical means of countering unmanned aerial, underwater and surface vessels and vehicles, autonomous land vehicles and other automated unmanned systems” have been added to an official list of weapons, ammunition and special gear. A 2005 government decree already allows postal employees to carry 9mm pistols, as well as stun guns and body armor. These weapons are typically given to security staff transporting cash. The expanded decree signed by Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin last Thursday does not specify which Russian Post workers will receive the anti-drone weapons. news Can ‘Russia’s Amazon’ Survive Ukraine’s Drone Campaign? title: Georgy Matyukhin, Russia’s First Central Bank Chief, Dies at 91
text: Georgy Matyukhin, Russia’s First Central Bank Chief, Dies at 91 Sep. 8, 2026 Georgy Matyukhin. wikimedia.org The first governor of Russia’s Central Bank after the fall of the Soviet Union, Georgy Matyukhin, has died at the age of 91. Russia’s Central Bank announced Tuesday that Matyukhin passed away on Saturday, one day ahead of his 92nd birthday. The regulator praised Matyukhin as an “active and responsible leader” who was appointed to lead the State Bank of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic “during a critical turning point” in 1990. “He oversaw the formation of the Bank of Russia under new conditions, leading it until 1992,” the Central Bank said in a statement. opinion How Russia’s Obsession With Economic Stability Made It Weaker Read more Matyukhin played a key role in the development of modern Russia’s financial sector during severe currency shortages and soaring inflation. Russian business media described one of his main achievements as the establishment of Russia’s two-tiered banking system, with separated central monetary authority from commercial banking operations. title: Hungary Expels 10 Russian Diplomats for ‘Unacceptable Activities’
text: Hungary Expels 10 Russian Diplomats for ‘Unacceptable Activities’ By AFP and Reuters Sep. 8, 2026 The Russian Embassy in Budapest. Aled Betts (CC BY 2.0) Hungary expelled 10 Russia n diplomats on Tuesday, saying they had acted in ways incompatible with their diplomatic status. Those kicked out "were engaged in activities in Hungary that are unacceptable for diplomats under the Vienna Convention," Hungarian Foreign Minister Anita Orban said in an emailed statement on Tuesday. Hungary has "called on the individuals in question to leave" the country, Orban said. She added that the action "does not imply breaking off diplomatic relations with Russia." "Hungary intends to continue the necessary dialogue, based on mutual respect and adherence to the rules," Orban said, without giving details of what the mission staffers had allegedly done. Russia 's Foreign Ministry said it would retaliate for the expulsion of its diplomats. "The response to the Russophobic lobby in Budapest will be harsh and painful," Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova told the state-run news agency TASS. title: Finland Completes Construction of Russian Border Fence
text: Finland Completes Construction of Russian Border Fence Sep. 8, 2026 The new border fence between Finland and Russia. raja.fi Finland has completed construction on a 200-kilometer (124-mile) fence along its eastern border with Russia, three years after the project began, the Finnish public broadcaster Yle reported Monday. Finnish Interior Minister Mari Rantanen presented the completed fence near a shuttered border crossing, saying the barrier addresses heightened security risks following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and could be extended further. “What we particularly need is EU funding for eastern member states so that projects like this can be financed,” Rantanen said. The new fence cost 356 million euros ($413 million), with an estimated 2-3 million euros for annual maintenance, according to Finnish border authorities. news Tension and Unease for Russians in Finland Amid Border Shutdown Read more The barbed wire fence spans Finland’s southeastern border with Russia and parts of its eastern flank. title: FSB Arrests Moldovan Suspected of Shooting Air Force General
text: FSB Arrests Moldovan Suspected of Shooting Air Force General Sep. 8, 2026 The Russian Investigative Committee Russia’s FSB security service said Tuesday that it arrested a Moldovan man who is suspected of shooting a Russian Aerospace Forces general on behalf of Ukraine last week. The FSB said its agents in the southern Astrakhan region arrested the man, identified as 21-year-old Nicolae Cociu. Investigators claim that Cociu shot a Russian serviceman near the Saratov region city of Engels last Thursday. While authorities did not identify the Russian serviceman by name, pro-Kremlin media reported last week that Major General Nikolai Varpakhovich, who heads a strategic bomber division at Engels-2 airbase, was shot and wounded in the Saratov region. In an official statement, the Investigative Committee, Russia’s top investigative body, confirmed the armed attack against the officer, who was hospitalized after receiving six gunshot wounds. A 39-year-old man was killed in an attack on a gas station in the Bryansk region town of Starodub, 35 kilometers (21 miles) north of the Ukrainian border, acting Governor Yegor Kovalchuk said . Three others were wounded, he added. In the nearby Belgorod region, acting Governor Alexander Shuvayev said one person was killed in a border district as a result of a “targeted” hit. Four others were injured across the region, where Shuvayev said Ukraine carried out 112 attacks in the past 24 hours. Unverified reports said that Ukrainian drones targeted a Rosneft-operated oil refinery in the southern Saratov region.
